fields.reasoning: Intent: the sibling change sets carved out of accepted umbrellas this session (code anchors 01M6HJX, unclaimed changes 01M6HKR) both serve model-tells-truth, and text-references' own statement (a rename never breaks a sentence) is about the model staying true; anyone-builds is the umbrella's broader root and adds nothing here. The carving guide says carve keeps IDs and links and that an emptied source is withdrawn by hand, and references-by-id is landed so the decided-by link applies in the target. Stored form: references-by-id says stored by ID, shown by handle; a bracketed @{ID} cannot collide with the '@' already in the log (emails, checkout@v7, '@key'), and requiring whitespace or ( [ before @ keeps those three from being read as references even on new writes. Verbatim fields are skipped because the hard rule is never to alter an owner's exact words, and sources are scrubbed transcripts. Refusing an unresolvable reference mirrors how a link to a node the write may not see is refused, and keeps a dangling reference from ever being written; @@ gives an escape so a literal @word can still be written. Resolving an input @{ID} like any reference, rather than passing it through as already-stored text, keeps a hand-typed @{BOGUS} from being stored unrefused; re-escaping a literal @ as @@ on display keeps a stored literal @word from being read back as a reference. Showing by current handle in both text and JSON makes output round-trip through a later write. A missing node in check is a fail because the capability exists so sentences never break, while a retired target is still a real node, so only a warn.
fields.statement: (1) Intent and leaf: the change set serves the landed root intent model-tells-truth, and the leaf comes over with rhiza carve text-references --from 01M5SWSWDVB237 --to 01M6HNNWFR1J2AHQRNKFTPME46, which keeps its ID and moves its decided-by link to references-by-id; the umbrella, left with no ops, is withdrawn. (2) Stored form and scanned fields: a write (node add or set) scans every string-valued field of a node, except the verbatim fields quote, quote_where and wording and every field of a source node, which are stored exactly as given. A reference starts with @ at the start of the text or after whitespace or an opening ( or [, followed by a handle (lower-case words joined by dashes), a node ID or unique ID prefix of 4+ characters, or the stored form {<full node ID>}; so emails, checkout@v7 and a quoted '@key' are not references. @@ writes a literal @ and is never resolved. Each reference is stored as @{<full node ID>}; an @{<ID>} in a write's input is a reference like any other, resolved and refused by the same rule, so hand-typed stored form cannot bypass resolution; json_fields and links are not scanned. Already-landed entries are never rewritten. (3) Unresolvable reference: the write is refused whole (not found, exit 4), naming each reference that names no node the write may refer to; the rule is the same as for a link's ends: landed nodes and nodes of the write's own change set, live and not retired. The error's next says to fix the handle or write @@ for a literal @. (4) Display and check: render, show, why, slice and the read apps (text and --json alike) show each @{ID} as @<the node's current handle> in that view and re-escape as @@ each stored literal @ that would otherwise start a reference, so the shown text written back in that view stores the same text; a reference that does not resolve in the view is shown as @{<full ID>}, and writing that back is refused like any unresolvable reference. rhiza check scans the folded model's stored references, each in the view of the change set that wrote it: an ID that names no node is a fail finding (a dangling reference), naming the node, field and ID; an ID that names a retired node is a warn.

fields.acceptance: Unit tests in internal/textref: a reference starts with @ at the start of the text or after whitespace or an opening ( or [ and is followed by a handle (lower-case words joined by single dashes) or an ID or 4+ character ID prefix; darin@hey.com, checkout@v7 and '@key' contain no reference; @@ yields a literal @ and is never a reference; a resolver given a lookup rewrites every reference, @{<ID>} included, to @{<full ID>} and returns each unresolved one with its offset, so @{BOGUS} is unresolved; a formatter shows @{ID} as @<handle> from a lookup and as @{<full ID>} when the lookup has none, and shows a stored literal @ that would start a reference (from @@word) as @@; a fuzz test checks that formatting resolved text, literal @ included, and resolving it again yields the same stored text
fields.statement: One pure package, internal/textref, finds the references in a text and turns them both ways: @handle, @<ID or 4+ character ID prefix> and @{<ID>} to stored @{<full ID>}, and stored @{<ID>} back to @<current handle>, with @@ for a literal @ both ways (the formatter re-escapes a literal @ that would start a reference)

fields.acceptance: text-refs-write.txtar: rhiza add capability with statement 'Builds on @other' stores @{<other's full ID>} in the log entry; an ID prefix reference stores the full ID; a reference to a node of the write's own change set resolves, one to a node of another unlanded change set or a retired node does not; quote, quote_where, wording and a source's fields are stored verbatim; '@@' stores a literal @; an input @{<other's full ID>} stores the same ID, and an input @{BOGUS} is refused like any unresolvable reference; an unresolvable reference exits 4 with code not_found naming each bad reference and its field, with a next saying to fix the handle or write @@, and writes nothing; --dry-run reports the same refusal; the same file through rhiza apply behaves the same; describe-golden.txtar is regenerated if a request or response type changes; the rhiza guide's skill text tells agents to write @handle to refer to a node
fields.statement: rhiza add and set, and add and set items of rhiza apply, resolve the references in every string-valued field of a node (except quote, quote_where, wording and every field of a source node) at write time and store each as @{<full ID>}, refusing the whole write when one names no node it may refer to

fields.acceptance: text-refs-display.txtar: after a node's statement refers to @other and other is renamed to renamed, rhiza show, rhiza why and rhiza slice print @renamed in markdown and in --json fields; rhiza render writes @renamed into the rendered page; a read app's --once JSON (rhiza tui app <read app> --once) shows @renamed; a reference to a node not in the view shows @{<full ID>}; a statement written with '@@word' stores a literal @word and is shown as @@word; copying the shown text into rhiza set stores the same text (same IDs, literal @ kept literal)
fields.statement: render, show, why, slice and the read apps, in text and --json alike, show each stored @{ID} as @<the node's current handle> in that view, and as @{<full ID>} when it does not resolve there, and show a stored literal @ that would start a reference as @@
